title: Order-Robustness Audit of Gradient Masking Methods for Continual Learning in LLMs

raw.stage1:
### Purpose:
The contribution's purpose is to test whether the published ranking of gradient masking methods holds under a different task ordering. Paper [24] ("The Effect of Task Ordering in Continual Learning") investigates the effect of task ordering on continual learning performance, showing that reordering tasks significantly affects catastrophic forgetting. This aligns with the contribution's purpose of examining task ordering effects, albeit in a broader context. Paper [16] ("Optimal Task Order for Continual Learning of Multiple Tasks") also explores task ordering, proposing strategies for optimizing it and analyzing its impact on learning performance. Both papers establish the empirical relationship between task ordering and performance, covering the purpose.

### Mechanism:
The contribution audits FGGM, MIGU, and an SFT baseline on TRACE under an alternative task order. Paper [1] introduces FGGM and compares it to magnitude-based methods like MIGU, describing the technical primitives of both approaches. Paper [19] ("Lookahead: a Far-Sighted Alternative of Magnitude-based Pruning") discusses magnitude-based methods, which are relevant to MIGU's mechanism. Paper [13] ("Prior Gradient Mask Guided Pruning-Aware Fine-Tuning") also uses gradient masking techniques, though in a different context. These papers collectively cover the mechanisms of FGGM and MIGU, as they describe substantively equivalent primitives.

### Evaluation:
The contribution evaluates ranking reversal using the TRACE benchmark under an alternative task order, reporting metrics like TRACE-OP points and seed-level performance. Paper [1] evaluates FGGM using continual learning benchmarks, including metrics for catastrophic forgetting, which aligns with the evaluation design. Paper [24] evaluates task ordering effects on continual learning performance using synthetic and naturalistic datasets, which is substantively equivalent to the evaluation design of the contribution. Paper [17] ("When Benchmarks are Targets") discusses sensitivity of LLM leaderboards to perturbations, including task ordering, and uses similar evaluation metrics to analyze ranking effects. These papers collectively cover the evaluation design.

### Domain:
The contribution operates in the domain of continual learning for LLMs, specifically focusing on gradient masking and the TRACE benchmark. Paper [1] addresses catastrophic forgetting in continual learning for LLMs, introducing FGGM as a solution. Paper [24] investigates task ordering effects in continual learning, which is part of the same application area. Paper [11] ("Elastic Variational Continual Learning with Weight Consolidation") also operates in continual learning for neural networks, addressing catastrophic forgetting. These papers cover the domain.
